Title: Modern neighborhood tour: getting around and public spaces
Description: A guided walk through a modern town: streets, cars, deliveries, libraries, parks and access for everyone, with questions at every stop.

Title: Ecological design tour: water, plants and shared land
Description: A guided tour of the Green World, a city that grows with the forest, and the real nature-based ideas behind it: clean water, wetlands, green roofs, meadows, compost and the commons.

Title: Robotic future tour: technology, energy and who decides
Description: A guided tour of an imagined Moon and Mars settlement: power, robots, self-driving vehicles, recycling and who makes the decisions.

Title: Heavenly City tour: the story of Jesus in ten stops
Description: A guided walk through the Heavenly City, the awaited city of gold and light, with a young guide, telling the story of Jesus as the Bible tells it, from the first garden to the empty tomb.

Title: Medieval town tour: castle, market and abbey
Description: A guided walk through a medieval town with a young mapmaker: the town gate, market day, guilds and crafts, the windmill, the abbey and the castle.

Title: Pyramid in Ancient Egypt: how it worked
Description: A giant stone tomb for a pharaoh. The Great Pyramid at Giza was the tallest building on Earth for about 3,800 years. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Aqueduct in Ancient Rome: how it worked
Description: A channel that carried fresh water from hills and springs many kilometers away into the city, using only gravity. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Medieval castle: how a king's fortified home worked
Description: A fortified home for a king or lord: thick stone walls, towers and a gate that could be shut tight. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Family house: why towns need it and how it works
Description: A detached house with a porch and garden, built for one household. It is the most common home in many countries. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Great tree hall: green idea, real nature technology
Description: A nature-inspired hall grown from a living tree. In the real world, people already shape living roots and trunks into bridges and buildings. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Pod home: how it could work on the Moon and Mars
Description: A compact home that could be launched folded up and inflated on arrival, giving astronauts much more space for its weight. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Tree of life in the Heavenly City: the story of Jesus
Description: A great tree with golden leaves and glowing fruit. The Bible begins and ends with a tree of life, and the story of Jesus begins here. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Great Sphinx in Ancient Egypt: how it worked
Description: A giant lion with the head of a king, carved out of the rock beside the pyramids of Giza about 4,500 years ago. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Public fountain in Ancient Rome: how it worked
Description: A stone basin on a street corner where anyone could collect fresh water from the aqueducts. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Gatehouse in a medieval town: how it worked
Description: A fortified gate between two towers, where guards decided who could come in and collected tolls. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Suburban house: why towns need it and how it works
Description: A house with a driveway and garage on the edge of a city, designed around travel by car. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Sunlight hall: green idea, real nature technology
Description: A nature-inspired hall that feeds on sunlight like a leaf. Real buildings already grow algae in their walls to make heat and fuel. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Moon base home: how it could work on the Moon and Mars
Description: Linked domes where a crew could live on the Moon, shielded from radiation and connected by pressurized tunnels. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Rainbow pavilion in the Heavenly City: the story of Jesus
Description: An open pavilion of flowers under a soft rainbow. In the Bible, the rainbow is a sign that God keeps his promises. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Obelisk in Ancient Egypt: how it worked
Description: A tall, four-sided stone pillar with a pointed top, cut from a single piece of granite and set up in pairs at temple gates. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Roman baths: hot, warm and cold rooms explained
Description: A huge bathhouse with hot, warm and cold pools where Romans washed, exercised, relaxed and met friends. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Watchtower in a medieval town: how it worked
Description: A lookout where watchmen kept an eye on the roads and the town, day and night. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Older brick house: why towns need it and how it works
Description: An older home that can be repaired and upgraded to use far less energy, instead of being knocked down. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Treetop village: green idea, real nature technology
Description: A nature-inspired village of homes and bridges among the branches, built so lightly that the trees stay healthy. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Life support dome: how it could work on the Moon and Mars
Description: The machinery that keeps air breathable, removes carbon dioxide and controls temperature: the beating heart of any space home. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Angel statue in the Heavenly City: the story of Jesus
Description: A golden angel with open wings on a tall column. In the Bible, the angel Gabriel told Mary that she would have a son, Jesus. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Cat statue in Ancient Egypt: how it worked
Description: A statue of a sitting cat, the sacred animal of the goddess Bastet. Egyptians loved cats, which kept homes and granaries free of mice and snakes. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Amphitheater in Ancient Rome: how it worked
Description: A giant oval arena where crowds watched animal hunts and gladiator contests. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Great hall in a medieval town: how it worked
Description: The big room at the heart of a castle or manor, where the household ate, met and held court. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Apartment building: why towns need it and how it works
Description: A building of several floors with many homes stacked together, sharing walls, stairs and services. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Tree tower home: green idea, real nature technology
Description: A nature-inspired tower wrapped in trees. Real "vertical forests" plant hundreds of trees on the balconies of city apartment blocks. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Printed shelter: how it could work on the Moon and Mars
Description: A dome-shaped home built by robots that 3D print walls from local soil, so heavy materials do not have to be launched from Earth. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Welcome hall in the Heavenly City: the story of Jesus
Description: A hall with a bed for every guest. When Jesus was born in Bethlehem, there was no room at the inn, so he was laid in a manger. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Pharaoh's palace in Ancient Egypt: how it worked
Description: The home and offices of the king. Egyptians called the palace per-aa, the "great house", and that word became our word "pharaoh". A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.

Title: Chariot racetrack (circus) in Ancient Rome: how it worked
Description: A long racetrack where crowds cheered for chariot teams racing around a central barrier. A free illustrated page for kids and teachers, with key words and questions to discuss.
